question: What is the simple definition of a nutrient?

options.A: Artificial supplements created in laboratories to boost immunity
options.B: Medical drugs prescribed strictly to cure infectious diseases
options.C: Waste products that the human digestive system must eliminate
options.D: Chemical substances obtained from food for body function and repair

explanation: Nutrients are simply the helpful components we get from our food that keep us growing, energized, and healing properly! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h1)

question: Why do clinical nurses need to understand the basics of diet and nutrition?

options.A: It allows nurses to support recovery and identify early malnutrition
options.B: It helps nurses prescribe complex surgical procedures independently
options.C: It replaces the need for professional hospital dietitians entirely
options.D: It enables nurses to manufacture synthetic vitamins at the bedside

explanation: Knowing your nutrition helps you spot early signs of poor feeding in patients and guide them toward a faster recovery! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h1)

question: Which food group is the body's main and quickest source of energy?
explanation: Carbs break down quickly into glucose, which acts as the favorite fuel for your cells and brain. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h2)

question: What is the main job of proteins in our diet?

options.A: Simple sugars utilized strictly for immediate brain activity
options.B: Inorganic elements that regulate body fluid balance
options.C: Fatty acids stored directly in adipose tissue for insulation
options.D: Amino acids used for tissue construction and cellular repair

explanation: Think of proteins as your body's building blocks. They break down into amino acids to fix worn-out tissues and build new ones. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h2)

question: How do vitamins mostly help our bodies work?

options.A: Forming the primary structural skeleton of human bones
options.B: Serving as concentrated thermal insulation beneath the skin
options.C: Providing the bulk energy needed for intense physical exercise
options.D: Acting as coenzymes to help biochemical reactions run smoothly

explanation: Vitamins don't give you direct energy like carbs, but they act like little sparks or helpers (coenzymes) to keep your body's chemistry running smoothly. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h3)

question: Calcium, potassium, and iron belong to which group of nutrients?
explanation: These are essential minerals! They help build strong bones, balance your body fluids, and carry oxygen in your blood. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h3)

question: Roughly what percentage of a healthy adult's body weight is water?
explanation: Water makes up about 60% of an adult body! It is the fluid highway where almost all cellular activities happen. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h4)

question: A patient who is severely dehydrated is most at risk of experiencing what?

options.A: Immediate thickening of bone tissue matrices
options.B: Rapid overproduction of red blood cells
options.C: Impaired kidney function and electrolyte imbalance
options.D: Excessive accumulation of dense adipose tissue

explanation: When water levels drop too low, blood volume decreases, placing stress on the kidneys and messing up vital body salts (electrolytes). [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h4)

question: What is the main difference between dietary fiber and other carbohydrates?

options.A: Fiber is an inorganic mineral rather than an organic compound
options.B: Human digestive enzymes cannot break down dietary fiber
options.C: Dietary fiber is absorbed directly into the bloodstream as starch
options.D: Fiber provides twice as many calories per gram as sugars

explanation: Unlike sugary carbs, fiber laughs at our digestive enzymes! It passes through our gut mostly unbroken. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h5)

question: How does insoluble fiber specifically help your tummy and bowels?

options.A: It acts as a primary coenzyme for protein synthesis in the liver
options.B: It dissolves completely in water to lower blood cholesterol
options.C: It adds bulk to stool and stimulates regular bowel movements
options.D: It provides direct thermal insulation for abdominal organs

explanation: Insoluble fiber adds weight and bulk to waste, keeping things moving smoothly so you don't get constipated. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h5)

question: Traditional red palm oil is especially rich in which nutrient helper?
explanation: Good old local red palm oil is packed with beta-carotene, which our bodies happily turn into Vitamin A for good eyesight and health. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h6)

question: Which common Nigerian food is a great plant-based source of protein?
explanation: Beans (cowpeas) are a fantastic, affordable local source of plant protein that helps build and repair body tissues. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h6)

question: Which physical sign is a classic clue that a patient might have iron deficiency anemia?
explanation: When iron is low, hemoglobin drops, making the inner eyelids (conjunctiva) look unusually pale instead of a healthy pink. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h7)

question: Why is a physical head-to-toe check important during a nutrition assessment?

options.A: It calculates the precise daily caloric expenditure during rest
options.B: It reveals visible deficiency signs like swollen gums or pale skin
options.C: It replaces the need for laboratory blood tests and dietary records
options.D: It accurately measures the exact percentage of body water volume

explanation: By simply looking at a patient's hair, skin, eyes, and mouth, you can often spot early physical clues of missing vitamins and minerals. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h7)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to recommend diet changes to a patient?

options.A: Focusing solely on vitamin supplements while ignoring whole daily meals
options.B: Tailoring suggestions to fit the patient's cultural background and food preferences
options.C: Insisting on expensive imported foods for guaranteed nutritional results
options.D: Providing a strict, unchangeable meal plan that ignores personal tastes

explanation: Patients will actually follow advice if it fits their lifestyle, pockets, and favorite local dishes instead of forcing foreign foods on them. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h8)

question: When teaching a patient about nutrition, which factor must you always keep in mind?

options.A: The brand name of hospital bed sheets
options.B: The specific color of the nursing uniform
options.D: The manufacturer of the IV infusion pump

explanation: Always consider what the patient can afford and find in their local market. A great meal plan is useless if they can't afford to buy the ingredients! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h8)
